nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ such that the number $k(G)$ of conjugacy classes of $G$ is greater than $|N|$ for every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The class number can exceed the order of every nilpotent subgroup

nodes.summary: The proposition that every finite group $G$ has a nilpotent subgroup $N$ whose order $|N|$ is at least the number $k(G)$ of conjugacy classes of $G$. This is Kourovka Problem 14.54 (M. W. Liebeck, L. Pyber).
nodes.title: Liebeck–Pyber problem on the class number and nilpotent subgroups

nodes.summary: There are an integer $k \ge 1$, an insoluble finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes, and a soluble finite group $G$ with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes whose order is at least the order of every finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes. So it is not true that whenever some insoluble finite group has exactly $k \ge 1$ conjugacy classes, every finite group of maximal order with exactly $k$ conjugacy…
nodes.title: A finite group of maximal order with a given class number can be soluble

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every integer $k \ge 1$ such that some insoluble finite group has exactly $k$ conjugacy classes, every finite group $G$ with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes whose order is at least the order of every finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes is insoluble. This is Kourovka Problem 17.77 (R. Heffernan, D. MacHale).
nodes.title: Heffernan–MacHale problem on groups of maximal order with a given class number
